title: Section equivalence identifies the canonical derived open adjunction
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion of schemes [def-weil-open-immersion]. Use small pro-étale sites small relative to the universe of module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For $T=U,X$, put $R_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], also denoting its reconstructed section-ring sheaf by $R_T$, and let $E_T:\operatorname{Mod}_{R_T}(\operatorname{Sh}(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\operatorname{Ab}))\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(R_T)$ be the fixed equivalence preserving underlying abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Use the coefficient isomorphism $\alpha_j:j^{-1}R_X\cong R_U$ [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]. Write $j_{!,\mathrm{int}}\dashv j^*_{\mathrm{int}}$ for the specified internal module adjunction [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek], and $j_{!,\mathrm{sec}}\dashv j^*_{\mathrm{sec}}$ for the specified section-module extension-by-zero/restriction adjunction of [def-pd-section-module-operations-data, lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. The localized site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] is identified with $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ by the site equivalence of Part (1) of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization].
The canonical comparison $E_Xj_{!,\mathrm{int}}\cong j_{!,\mathrm{sec}}E_U$ identifies the scalar actions on the sheafified extension presheaves [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf]: on the summand indexed by $\varphi:V\to U$, $r\in R_X(V)$ acts as $m\mapsto\alpha_j(r|_U)m$. Under this comparison and the canonical pullback comparison, the specified ordinary Hom bijections coincide, including their units and counits. Both extension and restriction are exact on both sides.
Use unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the induced section equivalences $D(E_T)$ and canonical pullback comparison $b:D(E_U)Lj^*_{\mathrm{int}}\cong Lj^*_{\mathrm{sec}}D(E_X)$ of [lem-pd-section-derived-pushpull-normalization]. Let $e_{\mathrm{int}}=D(j_{!,\mathrm{int}})$ and $e_{\mathrm{sec}}=D(j_{!,\mathrm{sec}})$ be the termwise localized extensions. Give $e_{\mathrm{int}}\dashv Lj^*_{\mathrm{int}}$ and $e_{\mathrm{sec}}\dashv Lj^*_{\mathrm{sec}}$ their independently specified adjunctions obtained by localizing the ordinary adjunctions [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction], with the right adjoints expressed through the canonical exact left-derived comparisons. Localizing the ordinary extension comparison gives $c:D(E_X)e_{\mathrm{int}}\cong e_{\mathrm{sec}}D(E_U)$. For every $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{R_U})$, $M\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{R_X})$ on the internal side, and $q:e_{\mathrm{int}}K\to M$, their specified derived Hom bijections $h_{\mathrm{int}},h_{\mathrm{sec}}$ satisfy
$$h_{\mathrm{sec}}\bigl(D(E_X)(q)\circ c_K^{-1}\bigr)=b_M\circ D(E_U)\bigl(h_{\mathrm{int}}(q)\bigr).$$
Thus these particular comparisons identify the canonical derived open adjunctions, including their units and counits, on all unbounded complexes.

source.place: Tags 03DI, lemma-extension-by-zero (summand action and adjunction Hom bijection), and 03DJ, lemma-extension-by-zero-exact; original Step 9 of lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison, including exact termwise localization of the specified open adjunctions.

proof.text: Apply Part (1) of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] to identify $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$; no constant-ring assertion in its Parts (2)--(3) is used for the condensed coefficient. Instead use the actual ring-object isomorphism $\alpha_j$ of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]. Write $A=E_U$, $B=E_X$, $J=j_{!,\mathrm{int}}$, $P=j^*_{\mathrm{int}}$, $J'=j_{!,\mathrm{sec}}$, $P'=j^*_{\mathrm{sec}}$. On the slice, inverse image of abelian sheaves is restriction. The module pullback formula of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] therefore identifies $P$ with restriction followed by scalar extension along $\alpha_j$. On an object $\varphi:V\to U$ the exact coefficient identification sends $a\otimes m$ to $a\cdot m$, where $m$ is regarded as an $R_U$-module element through $\alpha_j^{-1}$. Since $A,B$ preserve the underlying sheaves and restrictions, this is also the section-module pullback comparison $t:AP\cong P'B$ retained in [def-pd-section-module-operations-data]. Its inverse sends $m$ to $1\otimes m$.

source.place: Tag 04IX, definition-localize-ringed-site; coefficient identification as specified in the blueprint coefficient-morphism and module-pullback definitions

proof.text: Let $F$ be an internal $R_U$-module. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-extension-by-zero-presheaf-adjoint], its underlying abelian extension is the sheafification of the sum presheaf $\bigoplus_{\varphi:V\to U}F(V,\varphi)$. The underlying abelian extension of $JF$ is exactly this extension by [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek]. This identifies its underlying sheaf with that of $J'AF$, whose module presheaf is [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf]. Fix this identification by sending each presheaf generator $\iota_\varphi(m)$ to the same generator. The adjunction formula in the cited abelian lemma makes this the canonical identification: the inverse Hom map sends $a:F\to G|_U$ to the unique sheaf map with value $a_{(V,\varphi)}(m)$ on each generator. The unit on the slice sends $m$ to the generator indexed by the given structure map to $U$.

source.place: Tag 03DI, lemma-extension-by-zero, the direct-sum presheaf and both adjunction constructions

proof.text: Compute the scalar action of $JF$ on these generators. In [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] it is the inverse of the canonical abelian projection map followed by extension of the action of $\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_j}F$. The projection map is the adjoint-of-unit map of [sk-def-sfb-transport], Part (4). The unit from Step 2 sends $m$ to $\iota_\varphi(m)$, so on pure tensors that projection map sends $\iota_\varphi((r|_\varphi)\otimes m)$ to $r\otimes\iota_\varphi(m)$. This computes the actual projection map, not an arbitrarily chosen isomorphism; equality can be checked before sheafification since the tensor in [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] is sheafified objectwise tensor. Its inverse followed by the action thus sends $r\otimes\iota_\varphi(m)$ to $\iota_\varphi(\alpha_j(r|_\varphi)m)$, using the definition of restriction of scalars in [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. That is precisely the action in [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf]. The unique extension of the presheaf action to sheafification in [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] shows that the generator identification of Step 2 is $R_X$-linear and gives $c_0:BJ\cong J'A$.

source.place: Projection formula, linear extension, and coefficient restriction bullets; sites-modules.tex Tag 03DI, lemma-extension-by-zero, first proof paragraph, and Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules

proof.text: The ordinary adjunction Hom maps also agree under $c_0$ and $t$. Indeed, for $q:JF\to G$ its abelian adjunct on $(V,\varphi)$ sends $m$ to $q_V(\iota_\varphi(m))$ by [lem-weil-pbc-site-extension-by-zero-presheaf-adjoint]. It is linear for the restricted coefficient: $q_V(\iota_\varphi(\alpha_j(r|_\varphi)m))=r\,q_V(\iota_\varphi(m))$ by Step 3. The internal lifted adjunction of [sk-def-sfb-transport] and its invertible coefficient change [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] give this same map after the $1\otimes m\leftrightarrow m$ identification of Step 1. Conversely a linear map on the slice gives the map from the sum presheaf by this formula on every summand; it factors uniquely through module sheafification by [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. The two procedures are inverse because their composites fix every summand generator, respectively every section on the slice. Thus, writing $h,h'$ for the ordinary Hom bijections, $h'(B(q)c_{0,F}^{-1})=t_G A(h(q))$. In particular $c_0$ is the uniquely mate-normalized comparison retained in [def-pd-section-module-operations-data], rather than merely an isomorphism of the endpoint functors.

source.place: Tag 03DI, lemma-extension-by-zero, the maps alpha to alpha-prime and beta to beta-prime; the omitted inverse verifications are supplied here

proof.text: Denote the ordinary units by $\eta,\eta'$ and counits by $\varepsilon,\varepsilon'$. Substituting $q=1_{JF}$ into Step 4 and using $h(q)=P(q)\eta_F$ gives $\eta'_{AF}=P'(c_{0,F})\,t_{JF}\,A(\eta_F)$. Substituting $q=\varepsilon_G$ gives $\varepsilon'_{BG}\,J'(t_G)=B(\varepsilon_G)c_{0,PG}^{-1}$, since $h(\varepsilon_G)=1_{PG}$. These are exactly the unit and counit equations for the fixed comparisons. All compositions here and below are read right to left.

source.place: Tag 03DI, lemma-extension-by-zero; elementary specialization of the Hom identity from Step 4 to identities and counits

proof.text: Both section-module functors are exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], applied to the slice of Step 1 and the coefficient isomorphism $\alpha_j$. Changing coefficients along an isomorphism is an equivalence by [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], so it does not change exactness. On the internal side $J$ is exact by [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek], and $P$ is exact by [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main], with $f=j$. The section equivalences are exact by [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison]; its site-size and sheafified tensor hypotheses are the small-site convention of the statement and [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Thus these are additive exact functors between the module abelian categories; no injective or boundedness condition has been added.

source.place: Tag 03DJ, lemma-extension-by-zero-exact; exact restriction on the localized site; internal exactness is the cited module-pullback theorem

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to the exact functors of Step 6: their degreewise functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms and every complex represents their derived value. Apply [lem-sfb-adjunction-localization] to the degreewise ordinary adjunctions with the standard factorization isomorphisms. By [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction] these are the independently specified localized adjunctions, with units and counits given by the formulas of that lemma. Localize $c_0$ and $t$ to comparisons $c:D(B)D(J)\cong D(J')D(A)$ and $\bar t:D(A)D(P)\cong D(P')D(B)$. Existence and compatibility with composition of these localized transformations follow from Part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. This uses whole categories of unbounded cochain complexes, not only bounded-below or resolving representatives.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; adjunction descent and normalization formulas in Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Localization/Adjunction.lean:89,118,125

proof.text: Write $s:Lj^*_{\mathrm{int}}\cong D(P)$ and $s':Lj^*_{\mathrm{sec}}\cong D(P')$ for the canonical exact-functor comparisons used in the statement. Then the specified $b$ is $(s'D(B))^{-1}\bar t\,D(A)(s)$. To check this identification, precompose with cochain localization: the comparisons of [lem-pd-section-derived-pushpull-normalization] commute with the ordinary pullback comparison $t$ and the derived resolution comparison transformations. Because $P,P'$ are exact, every complex computes those functors by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]; the exact-functor comparison transformations are invertible and can be cancelled in that square. The result is precisely the localized component of $t$ on each complex. Part (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] then gives the displayed equality of natural transformations. This verifies the normalization of $b$ relative to $\bar t$; it does not choose a new pullback comparison.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor, and normalization by the factorization equations of the canonical derived pullback comparison

proof.text:
Localize the two equations of Step 5 degreewise. By the unit/counit normalization formulas in [lem-sfb-adjunction-localization] and the definition [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction], these give the unit and counit comparison equations on every localized cochain complex, with $\bar t$ and $c$. Part (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] extends each equation to the entire derived category. Re-express the right adjoints through $s,s'$ and use Step 8. With $\mathcal A=D(A)$, $\mathcal B=D(B)$, $L=e_{\mathrm{int}}$, $L'=e_{\mathrm{sec}}$, $R=Lj^*_{\mathrm{int}}$, $R'=Lj^*_{\mathrm{sec}}$, the resulting equations for the specified derived units and counits are
$$\eta'_{\mathcal A K}=R'(c_K)\,b_{LK}\,\mathcal A(\eta_K),\qquad
\varepsilon'_{\mathcal B M}L'(b_M)=\mathcal B(\varepsilon_M)c_{RM}^{-1}.$$
In particular the units and counits being compared are the localized original ones of the two independently given adjunctions.

source.place: Exact termwise adjunction localization, Tag 015F; natural-transformation descent as in Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Localization/Adjunction.lean:118,125

proof.text:
For any derived morphism $q:LK\to M$, use the unit equation of Step 9 and naturality of $b$ to compute
$$\begin{aligned}
h_{\mathrm{sec}}(\mathcal B(q)c_K^{-1})
&=R'(\mathcal B(q))R'(c_K^{-1})\eta'_{\mathcal A K}\\
&=R'(\mathcal B(q))b_{LK}\mathcal A(\eta_K)\\
&=b_M\mathcal A(R(q))\mathcal A(\eta_K)
=b_M\mathcal A(h_{\mathrm{int}}(q)).
\end{aligned}$$
The cancellation is $R'(c_K^{-1})R'(c_K)=1$. This is the requested identity. It applies to arbitrary derived morphisms; no representation of $q$ by a single cochain map was assumed. The second equation of Step 9 gives the counit compatibility, completing all the assertions.
